Thought: I need to determine how flammable chlorosilanes are. Chlorosilanes are compounds containing silicon-chlorine bonds, and I need to recall their chemical properties, particularly their flammability characteristics.

Chlorosilanes (compounds with Si-Cl bonds) are generally known to be highly reactive compounds. They react vigorously with water, producing hydrogen chloride gas and often igniting spontaneously when exposed to air. This spontaneous ignition in air is characteristic of pyrophoric substances.

Common chlorosilanes like trimethylchlorosilane, methyltrichlorosilane, and trichlorosilane are classified as flammable or pyrophoric materials in chemical safety data sheets. They can ignite without an external ignition source when exposed to air, especially the lower molecular weight chlorosilanes.

Based on my knowledge of chemistry, chlorosilanes are definitely not nonflammable (option C) or just slightly flammable (option D). They are not typically classified as explosive (option A) in the strict sense, though their reactions can be vigorous. The most accurate description would be option B - flammable or pyrophoric.
